entries.title: Gem Finder: define what makes a passage extraordinary
entries.notes:
Start from the researcher's idea of finding the Gems. Separate corpus distinctiveness, surprise relative to preceding replies, conceptual contribution, creative connections, complexity, expressive force and conversational influence. Keep rarity distinct from quality, and uncertainty distinct from originality.

First step: collect a few researcher-selected gems, ordinary passages and examples of empty profundity, with short explanations. Draft a small set of scoring axes and a review interface before preparing any new classifier calls.
entries.finish: An explicit rubric, attributed example set and reviewable pilot design with a way to compare each axis and inspect its outliers.

entries.title: Independently review topic scores against close reading
entries.notes: Develop the coding guidance on discovery material, then obtain independent readings of the reserved validation targets. Distinguish discussion, evoked experience, asserted experience and denial. Keep the 60 reserved lineages out of development reading, and retain disagreements rather than replacing original scores.
entries.finish: Attributed independent ratings, documented blinding and an agreement/error analysis against the existing JEV scores.
entries.blocker: Independent reader and finalized coding guidance needed.

entries.title: Freeze the first balanced factorial experiment
entries.notes: Choose the primary causal contrasts and precision target, then settle the model panel, disclosures, fresh-root allocation and scheduling. Treat the current six-model design and twenty-roots-per-cell illustration as a draft. Mixed local–cloud pairs, trios and external disruptors remain useful subsequent contrasts.
entries.finish: A separately versioned executable freeze with qualified participants, outcomes, analysis plan, seeds, finite budget and failure rules.
entries.blocker: Serving qualification, semantic validation and precision decisions remain pending.
